It is argues on behalf of the applicant that the statement of the victim under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and Section 164 Cr.P.C. are at variance.
There is no corroborative material in support of the prosecution case.
In the ossification test victim has been found to be 17 years.

He further submits that a margin of two years on either side can be given as has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in a case reported in (1982) 2 Supreme Court Cases 538, Jaya Mala Vs. Home Secretary, Government of Jammu & Kashmir and Others.

sentences.text: It is next submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the victim is in habit of lodging false cases against innocent persons under Section 376 Indian Penal Code.
One such case (Case Crime No.127 of 2004 under Section 376 I.P.C) referred in the rejection order, was lodged by the complainant where the victim was same.
There is another application submitted to the Superintendent of Police, Barabanki against on Ajay Kumar dated 29.4.2022.
Upon which investigation was directed in the matter and report was submitted on 9.5.2022.
The report depicts that the prosecutrix was married to one Dharamraj.
It is further submitted that she is of bad character and gone to Lucknow with Ajay Kumar and thereafter she was brought back by the Gram Pradhan Angraunda (Gufran) by counselling her.
The father of the prosecutrix committed suicide as he was fed up with her daughter.
The applicant has no previous criminal history.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail prayer, however, could not dispute the aforesaid facts. .

On due consideration to the submissions advanced, perusal of the record as also the facts that the applicant is languishing in jail since 11.1.2023; has no criminal antecedents, statement of the victim,
the delay of six months in lodging the First Information Report and the history of the complainant of lodging F.I.R. against other persons without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, I find it to be a fit case for enlarging the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant Sohbati be released on bail in aforesaid case crime number subject to his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court concerned with the following conditions:
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.

(iii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iv) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
